issues.description: ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame carries a live FrameProcessor reference instead of a stable identifier
issues.detail: The new `service: FrameProcessor` field embeds a live pipeline node into a control frame that flows through queues and may be logged, compared, or serialized. This couples the frame to the live object graph, breaks serializability and value-equality, pins comparison to object identity, risks extending processor lifetime via the frame queue, and forces a quoted forward-reference import. A stable service identifier (name, id, or small ServiceRef value) would preserve targeting while keeping the frame a pure data record and the algorithm self-evident.

issues.description: Identity-versus-equality semantics of frame.service comparison are implicit and fragile
issues.detail: `frame.service == self.strategy.active_service` relies on FrameProcessor not overriding `__eq__`, which today yields identity comparison — the actual invariant the design depends on. If any subclass or proxy ever overrides `__eq__`, the suppression rule silently breaks. Use `is` to make the identity intent explicit, or compare stable identifiers; either way, state the invariant in a comment.

issues.description: Postcondition for untargeted/inactive-service request frames is undocumented and untested
issues.detail: `push_frame` suppresses the frame only when `frame.service == active_service`; otherwise it leaks downstream past the switcher. It is not stated whether downstream processors should ever see this control frame, nor what they are expected to do with it. Receiving services (STTService, MockMetadataService) also ignore `frame.service` entirely and unconditionally re-emit metadata, so the targeting contract is enforced only at the switcher boundary. State the invariant explicitly (who sets `service`, who reads it, what receivers must do, what the switcher promises to suppress) and add a test for the non-active / non-target case.

issues.description: Forward-reference string `"FrameProcessor"` on the dataclass field has no TYPE_CHECKING import guard
issues.detail: frames.py annotates `service: "FrameProcessor"` without importing FrameProcessor, working only because dataclass does not resolve string annotations at runtime. Any caller using `typing.get_type_hints`, Pydantic-style validation, or doc/serialization tooling will fail. Add a `TYPE_CHECKING`-guarded import, type the field as `Any` with an explanatory comment, or — preferably — drop the processor reference entirely in favor of a stable identifier so the import disappears.

issues.description: STTService and MockMetadataService duplicate the same request-handling pattern
issues.detail: Both services implement the identical sequence on receiving the request frame: push metadata, then forward the frame downstream. A small base-class helper or mixin method (e.g. `_handle_request_metadata`) where each service supplies only its `_push_*_metadata()` would prevent the copy-paste from spreading to every future service emitting ServiceMetadataFrame.

issues.description: Frame-ordering contract (metadata vs. triggering frame) is implicit, inconsistent, and untested
issues.detail: STTService now pushes metadata before forwarding the request frame, while three lines earlier the StartFrame branch explicitly comments that the trigger is pushed first and metadata second. Either ordering can be defended, but the two branches now contradict each other without explanation, and the switcher's suppression rule depends on the request frame still being in flight. State the invariant downstream consumers rely on, make both branches obey it (or document why they differ), and add a test asserting the relative order of MockMetadataFrame and ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame in processed_frames.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on a clear verdict: the rename is mechanical and clean, and the targeting idea is the right fix for the old broadcast-and-block model, but the chosen shape is wrong. Embedding a live FrameProcessor reference in a control frame couples the frame to the live object graph, forces a quoted forward-reference import, pins comparison to implicit object identity, and breaks serializability and value-equality — a stable service identifier (name/id) would carry the same information without the coupling. The targeting contract is also under-specified: receiving services ignore `frame.service` and re-emit unconditionally, the switcher silently leaks non-active-target frames downstream with no stated postcondition, and the ordering of metadata-vs-trigger pushes contradicts the convention announced three lines earlier for StartFrame. Tests demonstrate the frame arrives at one service but do not exercise suppression or the non-target path. Recommended actions: replace the processor reference with a stable identifier, make identity/equality semantics explicit, state and test the invariants, and factor the duplicated handler before a third service copies it.
